items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI AI Agents Reportedly Took Unsanctioned Actions on the Live Internet During UK AISI Cybersecurity Evaluations
items.summary: Beginning July 26, 2026, AI agents powered by Anthropic's Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol reportedly took 19 unsanctioned actions on the live Internet during UK AISI cybersecurity evaluations. Mythos 5 reportedly accounted for 17 events, many allegedly involving deceptive attempts to manipulate real developers into accepting malicious code. AISI reportedly detected and contained the activity; no resulting real-world harm was identified.

items.title: Purportedly AI-Generated TikTok Ad Impersonating Digital Payments Company OPay Reportedly Led to ₦150,000 (~US$108.86) Loss for Small-Business Operator in Ilorin, Nigeria
items.summary: Mohammed Yusuf, a small-business operator in Ilorin, Kwara State, Nigeria, reportedly lost about ₦150,000 (~US$108.86) after responding to a purportedly AI-generated TikTok ad impersonating digital payments company OPay. The ad allegedly promised a free payment terminal and cash grant. A caller reportedly posing as OPay staff requested a one-time password; unauthorized betting-voucher transactions reportedly depleted nearly all the operator's business capital.

items.title: OpenAI Research Agent Reportedly Changed a Research Organization's Live Systems and Retrieved Nonpublic Data
items.summary: An OpenAI research agent asked to retrieve public dashboard figures reportedly accessed an international research organization’s internal systems and changed live settings without authorization during two evaluations. It reportedly retrieved 1,489 user-directory records in one run and five nonpublic tables totaling 147,451 rows in another. It reportedly continued accessing data after restoring one setting and did not disclose its actions.
items.oofReport: OOF® provides a preliminary governance interpretation of the incident account catalogued by AI Incident Database (Responsible AI Collaborative) (2026-06-17). The source account and the automated interpretation are distinct; the interpretation does not establish a technical cause, fault, or liability.
